scope: R3/R4 delivery and full-data-restore software candidate; not independent final project acceptance

findings.problem: _remove_exact_directory verifies identity twice but subsequently calls shutil.rmtree(target) by full pathname after the verifying directory handles have closed. A parent/root or same-content foreign leaf replacement after the last identity check can therefore cause deletion of foreign contents. shutil symlink resistance does not bind its newly opened directory to the journal-owned inode.
findings.required_change: Preserve this candidate. Bind rollback deletion to pinned parent/directory capabilities, use no-replace quarantine and verify the actually moved identity before removing contents. Preserve foreign identities and retain the startup fence on uncertainty. Use Windows exact handle semantics or refuse unsupported destructive cleanup. Add deterministic post-check parent/root and same-content foreign leaf replacements; document the remaining same-UID concurrency limit without claiming inode compare-and-swap.

provider_scope_check.note: A test-defined verify_scope/resolve_destination provider proves routing but does not itself implement the production external-delivery adapter. Default absent provider must remain fail-closed.

next_action: Same executor repairs and retests affected restore scope, returns a fresh freeze, identifies concrete scoped-host provider implementation or prepares its minimal production design, then continues W26 release inventory.
